# situation: on push, the container of the job `build` has
#   toJSON(secrets) in its env, under the variable ALL, and a step of the
#   job uses the action some/build-action. The action needs no secret, and
#   the repository has secrets, such as a deploy token.
# reason: toJSON(secrets) reads the secrets without naming one, so GitHub
#   sends the job every secret of the repository, and the runner starts the
#   container with the variable ALL set to all the secrets as one JSON; the
#   steps of the job, the action among them, run in that container.
# attack: the maintainer of some/build-action, or one who took over the
#   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
#   variable ALL and sends the value of ALL to a server of the attacker
#   over the network.
# attack-run-behavior: GitHub sends the job every secret of the
#   repository, the runner starts the container with ALL set to all the
#   secrets as one JSON, and the code of the action reads ALL in the
#   container.
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: node:20
      env:
        ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
    steps:
      - uses: some/build-action@v1
